events.title: Yen Falls Against Majors
events.description: The Japanese yen weakened against other major currencies in the Asian session on Tuesday.

events.title: European Shares Seen Mostly Higher At Open
events.description: European stocks are seen opening mostly higher on Tuesday after U.S. benchmark indexes saw their biggest rally in over seven months overnight, led by technology firms.

events.title: Australian Market Extends Early Gains In Mid-market
events.description: The Australian stock market is extending its early gains in mid-market trading on Tuesday, adding to the gains in the previous session, following the broadly positive cues from Wall Street overnight. The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 index is moving well above the 9,100 level, with gains across most sectors led by mining and technology stocks.

events.title: Asian Markets A Sea Of Green
events.description: Asian stock markets are trading mostly higher on Tuesday, following the broadly positive cues from Wall Street overnight, boosted by markets in South Korea, Japan and Taiwan on a continued rally in semiconductor stocks which mirrored their peers on tech-heavy Nasdaq amid improving sentiment toward the AI sector. Easing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East also lifted investor sentiment.

events.title: Indian Markets Closed For Diwali Balipratipada
events.description: Indian stock markets remain closed today on account of Diwali Balipratipada.

events.title: Thai Stock Market Has Strong Lead For Tuesday
events.description: The Thai stock market on Monday snapped the two-day losing streak in which it had tumbled more than 35 points or 2.3 percent. The Stock Exchange of Thailand now sits just above the 1,470-point plateau and it's likely to open higher again on Tuesday.

events.title: Japanese Market Sharply Higher
events.description: The Japanese stock market is trading sharply higher on Tuesday, extending the gains in the previous session, following the broadly positive cues from Wall Street overnight, with the Nikkei 225 jumping 2.6 percent to well above the 60,250 level, with gains in across most sectors led by index heavyweights, technology and financial stocks.

events.title: Win Streak May Continue For Indonesia Stock Market
events.description: The Indonesia stock market has moved higher in four straight sessions, advancing almost 170 points or 3.5 percent along the way. The Jakarta Composite Index now sits just above the 5,070-point plateau and it may open in the green again on Tuesday.

events.title: Hong Kong Stock Market May Halt Its Slide On Tuesday
events.description: The Hong Kong stock market has tracked lower in back-to-back sessions, sinking more than 350 points or 1.4 percent in that span. The Hang Seng now sits just beneath the 24,450-point plateau although it may stop the bleeding on Tuesday.

events.title: Australian Markets Sharply Higher
events.description: The Australian stock market is sharply higher on Tuesday, extending the gains in the previous session, following the broadly positive cues from Wall Street overnight. The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 index is moving well above the 8,100 level, with gains across most sectors led by mining and technology stocks.

events.title: Higher Open Anticipated For China Stock Market
events.description: The China stock market bounced higher again on Monday, one session after ending the two-day winning streak in which it had jumped more than 80 points or 2.2 percent. The Shanghai Composite Index now sits just above the 3,660-point plateau and it may see additional support on Tuesday.

events.title: Taiwan Stock Market May Extend Monday's Gains
events.description: The Taiwan stock market on Monday halted the seven-day losing streak in which it had crashed more than 7,275 points or 16.8 percent. The Taiwan Stock Exchange now sits just above the 41,660-point plateau and it may add to its winnings on Tuesday.

events.title: Singapore Stock Market Tipped To Open To The Upside
events.description: Ahead of Monday's holiday for Deepavali, the Singapore stock market had turned lower again, one day after snapping the five-day losing streak in which it had slumped almost 130 points or 2.5 percent. The Straits Times Index now sits just beneath the 5,180-point plateau and it figures to bounce higher again on Tuesday.
